A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the last glacial period was a time of major climate change in the Southern Hemisphere middle latitudes of South America, with a series of cooling events superimposed on a long-term trend of climate deterioration.

climate in the southern Chilean Andes was strongly linked with the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets, and that the last termination in middle latitudes of the Southern Hemisphere is characterized by at least two major phases of climate change, one of them involving a late-glacial reversal of climate trend that is synchronous with the Younger-Drya s in the Northern Hemisphere.

the glacial-interglacial transition of last-glacial time was characterized by a series of climate steps, with the initial step beginning at 14.6 14C ka, a second beginning at 13 14C ka and a late-glacial reversal of climate trend beginning near 12.2 14C ka.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Southern Hemisphere climate was much more sensitive to the glacial/ interglacial transition than the Northern Hemisphere climate.
climate in middle latitudes of the Southern Hemisphere during the last glaciations was strongly coupled to that in the Northern Hemisphere.
the climate signal from the Chilean Lake District is in phase with that from the Argentine Andes.
